title: PRINCIPLES OF FINANCIAL PLANNING
description: Provides an overview of professional approach to personal financial planning. Topics included are client/planner interaction, financial statement development and analysis, time value of money, cash flow and debt management, risk management, education planning, retirement planning, tax planning, estate planning, special needs planning, business entity selection and taxation, economics and external environment study, ethics and practice standards of Certified Financial Planner. Formulates a comprehensive financial plan that best fits a client while following ethics and professional responsibilities.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: BA 240, 240H, 360 or 360H.
A minimum grade of C- is required in BA 240, BA 240H, BA 360 and BA 360H.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman, Sophomore or Junior may not enroll.

Enrollment is limited to students with a program in Finance (182) or Finance (813).

Hybrid section; both on-site meetings and online component.
